root_motivation: Give the wintermute brain a read+act surface over the entire X11 desktop (not just the browser) so it can autonomously operate any app — text editors, file managers, settings dialogs — using AT-SPI accessibility semantics for reading and xdotool/baton for acting, with the same snapshot-with-refs mental model as wm-browser.
user_persona: jsy running wintermute on an Arch Linux X11 laptop; brain issues tool calls over agorabus and expects structured JSON replies shaped like wm-browser's protocol.

acceptance_criteria.description: `wm-desktop apps` returns JSON `{apps:[{name,pid,window_ids}]}` with at least one entry on a running X11 session; binary exits 0.
Protocol types (Command, Reply, AxNode, Snapshot, Tool enum) serde-roundtrip correctly and `tool_parse` covers all 7 variants plus unknown→None.
`cap_snapshot` truncates at 1500 refs and sets `truncated:true`; under the cap leaves `truncated:false`. Pure unit test, no AT-SPI required.
`find_matches` filters by case-insensitive text + optional role predicate; returns `[{ref,role,name}]` shape matching the protocol spec.

Daemon subscribes to topic `wm.desktop.cmd`, dispatches `apps`/`focus`/`read_window`/`click`/`type`/`key`/`find` commands, publishes replies on `wm.desktop.reply`. Unknown tool → `{ok:false,error:"unknown tool"}` rather than panic.
Binary compiles, `cargo clippy -D warnings` passes, `cargo deny check bans licenses sources` passes, `cargo test --workspace` exits 0.
`wm-desktop focus {app:"<name>"}` sets focus by resolving the window via AT-SPI app list; reply `{ok,window_id}`. Stub test (mock AT-SPI) verifies dispatch logic.
`wm-desktop type {text:"hello"}` delegates to `baton type "hello"` subprocess; captured subprocess invocation matches expected args. Test uses `--dry-run` flag or mock.
`wm-desktop key {combo:"ctrl+s"}` delegates to `baton key ctrl+s`; same mock/dry-run pattern as AC8.
`wm-desktop read_window` on the daemon returns a snapshot capped at 1500 nodes with `snapshot_id` UUID and `{ref,role,name,value,children_refs}` node shape.

scope: Binary `wm-desktop` daemon that subscribes to `wm.desktop.cmd` on agorabus
AT-SPI accessibility-tree reading via `atspi-connection` crate for `apps` and `read_window` tools
Snapshot-with-refs data model (1500-node cap, `{ref,role,name,value,children_refs}`) mirroring wm-browser shape
CLI one-shot mode: `wm-desktop <tool> [args]` prints JSON reply without daemon
`find` tool: text+role filter over the latest snapshot
non_goals: Wayland support — X11 only; revisit when hardware moves to Wayland
AT-SPI event streaming / subscription — only on-demand snapshot polling
Screen capture or OCR fallback — that is wm-screen-narrate's job
Native GUI or tray icon — pure headless daemon
Brain-side tool registration — the brain registers `desktop.*` tools separately
Auto-enabling the AT-SPI bus at install time — documented as manual step in README, not enforced by the binary

additional.note: atspi-connection pulls in zbus which is async/dbus-heavy; tokio runtime required. deny_unsafe holds because atspi-connection is safe Rust.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does the brain need an AT-SPI daemon beyond wm-browser?
five_whys_trace.a: wm-browser can only read/act on pages inside Chrome; the rest of the desktop (editors, file managers, dialogs) is invisible to it.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does the brain need to read and act on non-browser apps?
five_whys_trace.a: Vision §End-state #8 requires operating any app jsy might open — the brain can't achieve that with browser-only access; it would be locked out of 90% of the desktop.

five_whys_trace.q: Why use AT-SPI rather than screenshot+OCR for reading?
five_whys_trace.a: AT-SPI delivers semantic structure (roles, names, values, widget refs) that is both token-efficient and action-targetable; OCR gives raw pixels that must be re-parsed and can't produce reliable click refs.

five_whys_trace.q: Why mirror wm-browser's snapshot-with-refs shape instead of a custom shape?
five_whys_trace.a: The brain already knows how to handle snapshot-with-refs from wm-browser; a consistent mental model across surfaces eliminates the need for the brain to learn two different ref schemes.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Should the daemon auto-enable the AT-SPI bus if it is not running?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: No — auto-enabling requires writing autostart files and potentially restarting the session bus. This is documented as a manual prerequisite in README; the binary emits a clear error with instructions when AT-SPI is unavailable.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Which atspi crate: `atspi` (0.30) or `atspi-connection` (0.14)?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Use `atspi-connection` which provides the higher-level connection/proxy API; also add `atspi-common` for shared types. The monolithic `atspi` crate re-exports both but adds unwanted transitive deps.
